pattern.top_pattern: Multistate HMO acute hospital growth is concentrated in a few providers and high-acuity services
pattern.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual / HMO / Acute Hospital inpatient care across CA, CO, FL, GA, ME, NH, NV, NY, TX, and WI
key_driver_codes: Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours without MCC
pattern.pattern_details: Across this multistate HMO acute hospital segment, spend is rising through a mix of more admissions and higher paid per admit, with concentration in a few provider and high-acuity service line pockets. The pattern includes very high-cost craniotomy cases in GA, CO, and CA and a major provider pocket at Aurora in WI. Because several pockets are low-baseline and small volume, the right response is targeted exceptions management rather than broad program changes.
pattern.why_it_matters: A handful of provider-service line combinations are driving disproportionate HMO inpatient growth across multiple states.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Target provider-specific contract and UM review for Aurora in WI and the highest-cost craniotomy and sepsis admissions in GA, CO, CA, and TX, using case-level exceptions rather than broad benefit changes.
evidence_summary: This multistate HMO acute hospital segment added about +$7.5M.
AURORA MEDICAL CENTER - SHEBOYGAN COUNTY in WI contributed about +$0.9M on 40 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $23.5K.
Craniotomy with MCC added about +$1.4M in GA and +$1.3M in CO; a CA pocket shows about +$0.8M from only 2 added admissions.
TX sepsis added about +$0.6M with 20 more admissions.
